project: UI Factory Document vs Snapshot Planes (U4 Recovery v2)
description: Recovery retrigger for U4: separate the session factory document plane (React Query, authoritative for edit/save/export) from the dashboard event snapshot plane (timeline, authoritative for live runtime overlay), with documented authority rules, graph editor alignment, session-switch cache policy, after-save convergence, and export on the document plane.

context.customerAsk: Retrigger; prior token blocked on failed U2 recovery plan. Program note: also requires ui-session-factory-client-recovery (v1) complete before implementation; backend S1 complete. Full spec: tasks/prd-ui-factory-document-snapshot-planes.md
context.problem: The dashboard mixes React Query session factory documents with SSE DashboardSnapshot data. The graph editor, staleness checks, session switches, post-save refresh, and export can read or write the wrong plane, causing saves and displays to diverge when live runtime and editable definition differ.
context.solution: Document a two-plane authority model, then enforce it: document plane owns edit/save/export structure; snapshot plane owns live runtime overlay and in-flight guards; session switch resets document queries; save success updates document cache and converges snapshot without fetch storms; export uses session factory GET.

acceptanceCriteria: Editing and saving in one session never uses another session's DashboardSnapshot.factory as the sole save payload source when a document is loaded.
Graph edit mode seeds draft structure from the session factory document GET, not snapshot topology alone.
Session tab switch does not show the previous session's factory definition after loading completes.
Successful graph save updates the document cache and converges with the timeline without manual reload or unbounded refetch loops.
Export uses session-scoped factory document GET, not snapshot-only payload.
Dev guide section documents factory document vs dashboard snapshot authority with diagram.
Typecheck, lint, and make ui-test pass.

userStories.description: As a graph editor user, I want the editable graph structure to follow the loaded session factory document so my edits match what will be saved.
acceptanceCriteria: Entering graph edit mode with a loaded document shows nodes and edges from that document; while document GET is pending, editor shows loading or unavailable—not snapshot topology as the editable baseline.
useEditableFactoryGraph sets draft baseDocument and latestDocument from useCurrentFactoryDocument only; snapshot.factory is not assigned into draft baseline fields.
Vitest proves divergent document vs snapshot fixtures: editing uses document workstations, not snapshot-only extras.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify in browser using dev-browser skill: open graph editor and confirm structure matches persisted document after load

userStories.title: Snapshot limited to runtime overlay
userStories.description: As an operator watching a live factory, I want observe mode to reflect runtime overlay signals without treating snapshot topology as the save source of truth.
acceptanceCriteria: Observe mode may render live snapshot projection for display; switching to edit mode re-baselines on the document plane.
Save-blocked and stale-draft messaging uses document version plus snapshot in_flight_dispatch_count, not snapshot factory version alone.
activeWorkCount and in-flight save guard come from snapshot runtime, not document GET.
Vitest proves save payload is built from latestDocument or pending draft, never DashboardSnapshot.factory alone when document is present.

Tests pass
